bullet_feedback.bullet: Precomputed popular workflows from a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table into a Redis-cached category tree to keep lookups within the database's permission and rate limits, which became the Claude skill's main search tool
bullet_feedback.problem: Three unexplained ideas are packed into one sentence: 'category tree', 'permission and rate limits', and 'the Claude skill'. I can't tell what problem the limits caused (was the tool blocked, slow, or not allowed to query directly?) or who benefited.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: I can't pass this to a hiring manager without guessing, so the second Capital One bullet adds nothing to my screen beyond the word 'Redis'.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what went wrong when the AI tool queried the database directly (blocked by permissions, throttled, too slow), stated before the fix
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the constraint in plain words, then the fix, then that it became the main search tool; drop either 'PostgreSQL' or 'Redis-cached' from the sentence if the Skills line already carries it.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Designed the order book with std::list FIFOs per price level in a std::map and an order-ID hash map to make cancels O(1), which ran the full replay at 1.26M events/sec and hit a 1.2 µs p99 on a separate 2M-event run
bullet_feedback.problem: The first half is a stack of four C++ type names ('std::list FIFOs per price level in a std::map and an order-ID hash map') before the reader learns the goal ('make cancels O(1)'). The numbers at the end are strong but come after the hardest part to read.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A recruiter's eye stalls on the type names and may miss 1.26M events/sec, which is the number an HFT screener is looking for. An engineer will understand it either way.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Put the purpose (instant cancels, orders kept in arrival order at each price) before the data-structure names, or name the structures in plain terms ('a queue per price level, plus a lookup by order ID').

bullet_feedback.bullet: Cut AI workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by splitting a Claude skill into focused sub-skills that call Python search and validation tools instead of relying on open-ended model search
bullet_feedback.problem: 'AI workflow generation' and 'Claude skill' aren't defined: I don't know what a workflow is here or who generated them.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The 65% / under 15s result is clear, but without knowing what was being produced I can't say whether it mattered. It reads as an internal AI experiment.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what a 'workflow' is in this tool, in a few words
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Add a short noun phrase saying what the generated workflows are; shorten 'instead of relying on open-ended model search' to make room.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built Redis caching in front of Tortuga's Prisma ORM queries to reduce database load and latency for a class scheduler that drew 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days
bullet_feedback.problem: 'Tortuga' is never introduced. Is it the product, the company, or a library? 'to reduce database load and latency' states intent with no result, so the only number (20,000+ visits) describes traffic, not this work.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: I can't tell if Tortuga is the class scheduler or something else, and the bullet reads as 'added a cache' with no evidence it helped.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: whether Tortuga is the class scheduler's name; any measured effect of the cache, if one exists
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Name the product once in plain terms ('Tortuga, our class scheduler'), and cut 'Prisma ORM' from the bullet since it doesn't explain the engineering.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research documents to inference by replacing S3 staging hops with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda
bullet_feedback.problem: The heading 'UMD App Development Contracting (Client: Amazon Leo)' doesn't explain what Amazon Leo is, and 'routing ... to inference' and 'S3 staging hops' are jargon. The bullet is clear to an engineer, but I could misread who the employer was.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: If a recruiter suspects the Amazon name is being borrowed, they may discount the whole entry, even though the bullet is solid.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: that Amazon Leo is Amazon's satellite internet program (if that's correct), so the client is recognizable
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep the heading structure and swap 'to inference' for 'to an ML model'. The tech names can stay because they are the change.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built and prompt-tuned a pipeline for a PhD-led robotics project aimed at ICLR that overlays AnyGrasp's candidate grasps on camera images in Open3D to help a vision-language model pick grasps that avoid hitting the table
bullet_feedback.problem: This is the longest bullet in Experience and stacks two tool names (AnyGrasp, Open3D) between the setup and the purpose. It also has nothing to do with the low-latency target.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: It takes up two full lines in a section the HFT reader will skim past. That's minor, but it competes with the stronger systems evidence.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Trim to the purpose and method (draw candidate grasps on images so the VLM avoids collisions), and move 'Open3D' to Skills if it's needed.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Traced an apparent 1.65x regression to the CPU frequency governor with perf counters and a do-nothing control book to rule out a code change, which led to core pinning that cut run-to-run variance from 6% to 0.06%
bullet_feedback.problem: 'do-nothing control book' is a coined phrase that a non-engineer, and maybe some engineers, will stumble on. The 'which led to' chain makes it one long breath.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is a strong debugging story for HFT. The odd phrase is the only spot where a reader has to re-read it.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Rephrase 'do-nothing control book' as a plain description, e.g. 'a baseline build that did no matching work', keeping the rest as is.

page_feedback.problem: All the low-latency C++ evidence sits in one summer project. Every Experience entry is cloud, AI tooling or ML, so after the top block the page reads as 'cloud/AI engineer' rather than 'systems engineer'.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: An HFT screener may see one strong project plus unrelated internships and ask whether the C++ work was a one-off. The intended 'repeatedly built performance-sensitive systems' story only partly comes across.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Within existing facts, lead each Experience bullet with its performance or systems angle (latency, caching, capacity bounds), as the Leo and TerpLabs bullets already partly do.

page_feedback.problem: About the bottom 15% of the page is blank, while the body text is fairly small and the bullets wrap to two dense lines.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: The page looks denser than it needs to, and the extra space could make it easier to read.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Use the free space for slightly larger body text or more spacing between entries instead of adding content.

page_feedback.problem: Several bullets chain clauses with 'which ...' ('which agreed with', 'which ran', 'which showed', 'which led to', 'which became'). It happens five times across the page.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: The repetition makes it sound templated and makes bullets feel like one long run-on sentence when read aloud.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Split a couple of the 'which' clauses into a second short clause or vary the connector. Don't change any facts.

page_feedback.problem: The AWS internship (the biggest brand, and current) has a single present-tense bullet with no outcome, so it reads lighter than the Capital One entry below it.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: On a skim, the top-brand role gets the least attention. This is an accepted trade-off because results are still preliminary.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Leave as is; just keep the bullet in plain words. It already is.
